Eligibility 1. Eligible Applicants

 This Appendix is open to all categories of U.S. organizations, providing they have successfully completed, or are actively completing, a NIAC Phase I study that has not previously received a Phase II award. NIAC Fellows or their designees of the predecessor NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts are no longer eligible to submit Phase II proposals based on those prior Phase I studies. To be eligible for this solicitation, Phase I final reports must be submitted to the NIAC Program Office, e.g., emailed to hq-niac@mail.nasa.gov, by the Phase II proposal due date and time. If the Phase I final report is not received by this date and time, the submitted proposal will not be reviewed, and proposers will need to submit to a future NIAC Phase II solicitation. Individuals proposed to receive NIAC funding must be affiliated with a U.S. organization. Individuals not affiliated with a U.S. organization must receive a Unique Entity Identifier and Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code from SAM.gov prior to NIAC proposal submission. Non-U.S. organizations may participate in NIAC studies on a no-exchange of funds basis, and subject to NASA’s policy on foreign participation (see SpaceTech REDDI Section B.3 for additional information).

 Proposals that had previously been declined for award may be resubmitted, consistent with the requirements of this solicitation. Offerors planning to resubmit a non-selected proposal are encouraged to identify and address prior reviewer comments in their resubmitted proposal.

Proposals received after the submission deadline of June 12, 2026, 5 PM ET, will not be accepted for review. In such cases, offerors may consider submission to a future NIAC Phase II solicitation. Therefore, proposers are strongly encouraged to familiarize themselves with the NSPIRES system and begin the submittal process early, well in advance of the deadline.

NIAC Phase II seeks proposals that will continue the exploration and development of revolutionary advanced concepts started through a NIAC Phase I award. Application Review Information 1. Application Evaluation Criteria

 The following criteria will be used to evaluate proposals and inform selections. These evaluation criteria supersede the criteria defined in SpaceTech REDDI 2026 section F.1. All criteria are of approximately equal weight. Offerors shall address each criteria below to make the most compelling case for the proposed concept.

 NIAC Phase II Evaluation Criteria #1 Concept Progression a. The proposed research objectives build on the Phase I study findings while also

 demonstrating unexplored, exciting, and valuable aspects to investigate beyond the Phase I study.

 b. The analysis completed in Phase I is credible. However, unknowns remain that are not readily determined, thereby warranting further study.

 #2 Technical Study Approach a. A work plan is proposed that demonstrates an understanding of major issues and proposes a

 logical, strategic, and judicious course of study to address significant unknowns, barriers, and necessary technology development.

 b. The proposed study and its products are likely to significantly advance NASA’s understanding of concept feasibility and benefit.

 c. The work plan includes analysis of one specific mission demonstrating the potential for substantial benefits relative to the state of the art, or the enabling of an entirely new and highly appealing mission capability. d. Team members are sufficiently well qualified, and adequate resources are identified to complete the study as proposed.

 e. The study timeline is commensurate with the scope of the proposed budget. There is sufficient budget for labor, materials and supplies, mandatory travel, etc. to complete the study.15

 FY 2026 NIAC Phase II Appendix to SpaceTech REDDI 2026

 

 

 f. A plan to develop a technology roadmap has been adequately described and there is a mechanism for identifying the enabling technologies, which culminates in a feasible implementation of the concept.

 g. The proposed study continues the science or technology developed from the NIAC Phase I Award based on the provided Key Findings.

 #3 Representative Mission a. The proposal describes a specific representative mission in sufficient detail to enable the

 assessment of proposed technology benefits by a cognizant reviewer, to include rough preliminary estimates of total system mass, power and volume. A list of missions that may benefit from the innovation is not sufficient.

 b. The underlying mission architecture is technically sound, with at least one plausible implementation path identified and discussed.

Application Review Information 1. Application Evaluation Criteria

 The following criteria will be used to evaluate proposals and inform selections. These evaluation criteria supersede the criteria defined in SpaceTech REDDI 2026 section F.1. All criteria are of approximately equal weight. Offerors shall address each criteria below to make the most compelling case for the proposed concept.

 NIAC Phase II Evaluation Criteria #1 Concept Progression a. The proposed research objectives build on the Phase I study findings while also

 demonstrating unexplored, exciting, and valuable aspects to investigate beyond the Phase I study.

 b. The analysis completed in Phase I is credible. However, unknowns remain that are not readily determined, thereby warranting further study.

 #2 Technical Study Approach a. A work plan is proposed that demonstrates an understanding of major issues and proposes a

 logical, strategic, and judicious course of study to address significant unknowns, barriers, and necessary technology development.

 b. The proposed study and its products are likely to significantly advance NASA’s understanding of concept feasibility and benefit.

 c. The work plan includes analysis of one specific mission demonstrating the potential for substantial benefits relative to the state of the art, or the enabling of an entirely new and highly appealing mission capability. d. Team members are sufficiently well qualified, and adequate resources are identified to complete the study as proposed.

 e. The study timeline is commensurate with the scope of the proposed budget. There is sufficient budget for labor, materials and supplies, mandatory travel, etc. to complete the study.15

 FY 2026 NIAC Phase II Appendix to SpaceTech REDDI 2026

 

 

 f. A plan to develop a technology roadmap has been adequately described and there is a mechanism for identifying the enabling technologies, which culminates in a feasible implementation of the concept.

 g. The proposed study continues the science or technology developed from the NIAC Phase I Award based on the provided Key Findings.

 #3 Representative Mission a. The proposal describes a specific representative mission in sufficient detail to enable the

 assessment of proposed technology benefits by a cognizant reviewer, to include rough preliminary estimates of total system mass, power and volume. A list of missions that may benefit from the innovation is not sufficient.

 b. The underlying mission architecture is technically sound, with at least one plausible implementation path identified and discussed.
